originalGroup.material:
A call to the camera shop

Man: Hill Road Camera Shop. How can I help?
Zoe: Hello. I left a small bag in your shop yesterday. Have you found one?
Man: We have two bags here. What colour is yours?
Zoe: It is grey, with a yellow star on the front.
Man: Yes, I can see it. What is inside?
Zoe: A notebook and a pair of red gloves. There is no camera in it.
Man: That matches this one. Please bring something with your name when you collect it.
Zoe: Can I come at six this evening?
Man: We close at five thirty today. We open again at nine tomorrow.
Zoe: I have school tomorrow morning. Could Mum collect it for me?
Man: Yes. Please give her your name and the description of the bag.
Zoe: She can come at four today. Thank you for keeping it safe.
Man: You’re welcome. We will keep it behind the counter.

originalGroup.material:
Calling about a farm visit

Woman: Green Lane Farm. Good morning.
Ali: Hello. Our family would like to visit on Sunday. What time do you open?
Woman: At ten. The last entry is at three, and the farm closes at four.
Ali: Can we see the goats being fed?
Woman: Yes. That happens at eleven, near the red barn. Please watch with a staff member. Visitors must not give the animals their own food.
Ali: My sister is five. Does she need a ticket?
Woman: Yes. Children under four are free. A child ticket is four pounds, and an adult ticket is seven.
Ali: Can we bring lunch?
Woman: Yes. Use the picnic tables by the pond. The café also sells sandwiches.
Ali: What if it rains?
Woman: The farm still opens, but some paths may be muddy. Wear suitable shoes. If there is dangerous weather, we announce a closure on our booking page.
Ali: Thank you. We will check before leaving home.

originalGroup.material:
The moon in the puddle

In this story, a young fox sees the moon reflected in a puddle. He thinks it has fallen from the sky. He runs to Owl's tree and calls for help.

Owl looks up. The real moon is still above the hill, but Fox is staring at the water. "Look carefully," says Owl. Before she can explain, Fox fetches a small bucket.

He lowers it into the puddle. The water shakes, and the bright circle breaks into many moving pieces. Fox is worried that he has broken the moon. He sits down so suddenly that his tail splashes into the water too.

Owl waits until the puddle is still. The circle comes back. She asks Fox to look up, then down. At last he sees the two bright shapes together.

"One moon, two views," he says slowly.

Fox puts the bucket away. On his walk home, he sees the moon in a window and again in the river. This time he does not call for help. He counts the places where its light appears, while the real moon travels above him.

originalGroup.material:
The little post bell

In this fictional village, Rabbit delivers letters along a narrow lane. Every house has a small box by the gate. Rabbit usually leaves a letter and rings a bell to tell the family it has arrived.

One morning, the bell at Hedgehog's gate makes no sound. Rabbit taps it twice, then leaves the letter safely in the box. He decides to mention the silent bell when he returns.

That afternoon, Hedgehog is waiting outside. "I wondered when you would come," she says. She has been expecting a letter from her sister. Rabbit points to the box, and Hedgehog finds the envelope inside.

"The letter was here all along," she says. "I listened for the bell instead of looking."

They inspect the bell together. A piece of dry leaf is caught inside. Hedgehog removes it, and the bell rings again. She thanks Rabbit for delivering the letter even when the signal failed.

The next day, Rabbit still rings the bell. Hedgehog enjoys its familiar sound, but she checks the box too. The bell is useful news about a delivery; it is not the letter itself.

originalGroup.material:
Four family outings

The town visitor office offers four outings. The prices below are per person. Each outing must be booked before Friday noon.

| Outing | Time | Age | Price | Important information |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Canal Boat | Saturday 10:00–11:30 | All ages | £8 | Children under 12 must come with an adult. Life jackets supplied. |
| Hill Walk | Saturday 14:00–16:30 | 10 and over | £5 | Bring water and walking shoes. Uneven ground; no pushchairs. |
| Puppet Theatre | Sunday 11:00–12:00 | All ages | £6 | Indoors. Seats reserved at booking. No food during the show. |
| Garden Trail | Sunday 14:00–15:30 | All ages | £4 | Outdoor picture clues. One adult must accompany each family group. |

An adult needs a ticket as well as a child. Prices do not include travel to the starting point. Arrive fifteen minutes before the listed start. The office will contact booked visitors if an outing is cancelled. Boat and walking outings may change in unsuitable weather; the indoor show is unaffected by rain. Ask about access needs before paying, since the routes and venues differ.

originalGroup.material:
Where to ask for help

During the school open day, four help desks provide different services. All are free to use. Students should stay with their visiting family unless a teacher has agreed otherwise.

| Desk | Place | Open | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Welcome | Main gate | 9:00–12:00 | Gives maps and the day’s programme. |
| Lost Property | Library entrance | 10:00–14:00 | Holds found bags, coats and small items. Describe an item before collecting it. |
| Club Information | Sports hall | 9:30–13:30 | Explains club activities and future joining dates. Does not collect payments. |
| Quiet Space | Room 6 | 9:00–14:30 | Offers a place to sit away from the busy halls. A staff member is present. |

The open day begins at 9:00 and ends at 14:30. Lunch is sold in the dining room from 11:30 to 13:00. It is separate from the free help-desk services. Visitors who find an item should take it to Lost Property after 10:00; before then, give it to a teacher at Welcome. For an urgent problem, ask the nearest member of staff instead of waiting for a particular desk to open.
